items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: he's the first one that showed me how to finger saxophone

ctx.x: Earl Pearson, that's his name. Yeah. Bright, bright fella. Yeah. And he showed me the finger on the saxophone. Alto saxophone? Yeah. And I started playing the saxophone. Then I had a saxophone three weeks on. I played my first job. Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…
Well, too, John Henry, we're talking about Earl Piffson, you say something about him?

Yeah, he's the first one that showed me how to finger saxophone. From then on, I had, like I said, I had it on three weeks and I would play my first job. And there was no set up either because I would play it at the Entertainer's Cavalry. All the musicians come. All Creed and all Colour went there. Jammed back all night. What was that? It was on Basin Street, Basin between Iverville and Bainville. There was a place, John Henry, I'll talk about that, the Entertainer's Cavalry.
